We glanced at each other sideways. Writing bullshit on a computer screen. Crawling along the edge of a straight razor…and surviving. [...]
item.content:encoded:
Thou shalt not covet has always been funny to me, there’s nothing more human.

“I was born and raised in Calgary, but I live in a van in Amarillo Texas.”  There was a pause.  We glanced at each other sideways.

Writing bullshit on a computer screen.  Crawling along the edge of a straight razor…and surviving.  Time…space…I think I need counselling to stop watching the lady on French Food At Home and singing the theme song to myself when I’m not.

It’s hard to get inspired when you’re not out colliding yourself with the world, but that will recommence in exactly one month.  In the meantime, here’s some macro photos I took in Calgary.

item.title: Deja-vu All Over Again
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: It’s hard to describe the sheer elation I feel being in the exact same spot in Vancouver I was a year ago. Then I was just coming to grips with my newfound powers, ranting about self-actualization, feeling out the true boundaries of being free as a bird. 4000 miles and 365 days later, I still [...]
item.content:encoded:
It’s hard to describe the sheer elation I feel being in the exact same spot in Vancouver I was a year ago.  Then I was just coming to grips with my newfound powers, ranting about self-actualization, feeling out the true boundaries of being free as a bird.  4000 miles and 365 days later, I still feel somewhat the same, except now more seasoned and in control of exactly how far I can go.  The answer…far.

Vancouver's a hell of a town

Nothing has changed on Broadway Street in Kitsilano save a new dollar store or two opening.  I walk by a Mexican restaurant two blocks away and think to myself that I’d like to try it sometime, then hear echoes of me saying the exact same thing last summer.  Except this time I know how to cook Mexican and would be willing to bet I can do just as good a job.

One of my favourite self-quotes of life advice from the last time I was here was “get rich and piss it all away.”  I obviously haven’t been doing the pissing part properly because I still have enough coin to last for multiple more years when I return to Amarillo in September.  In reality I’ve probably got one more year in me, do the complete loop through the Mississippi river delta, Florida keys and eastern seaboard then be done with it.  I might only make it one if I had to stay in Vancouver and deal with $7 pints and 12% sales tax on everything.  Goddam socialists.

And now there’s a new career path I could start investigating…professionally entering social media intern contests.  I mean in hindsight the Stampede one wasn’t that hard.  Make 1 minute video, vote, win.  Drink, ride horses, tweet about stuff.  Bam, done.  Everyone’s telling me to get the resume updated with that on there, and funnily enough it definitely counts as a job, although I wouldn’t call it working.  And if I felt the need to be sending my resume around Calgary (not gonna happen, don’t worry) I’d get all kinds of bonus street cred if only out of curiousity, whether being a social media intern was applicable to the job or not, at least it proves I’m a real person.

And it’s funny I still feel the need to validate that, perhaps now more than ever.  Blimpy Backgammon, human being.  For all the firebrand vitriol and enlighten thineself this that and the other thing, all I can really ever change is whether I’m sitting or standing, eating or drinking.  And right now I’m going to go sit in the sun and drink a beer.

You want my advice?  Do whatever the fuck you want all the goddam time, that’s all there is to it.

item.title: Calgary Stampede 2011: Staring at the Sun
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: After leaving my temporary RV home on the Stampede grounds last Monday, it took all the way until Thursday until my brain started remotely working correctly. I was sitting on the front porch in my aviators staring at the sun when I realized all my neurons were firing in the correct order, and it scared [...]
item.content:encoded:
After leaving my temporary RV home on the Stampede grounds last Monday, it took all the way until Thursday until my brain started remotely working correctly.  I was sitting on the front porch in my aviators staring at the sun when I realized all my neurons were firing in the correct order, and it scared me.

About as close as it gets

For those expecting my usual incendiary tone or some sort of expose on how the Stampede really works, I’m afraid that will be hard to provide.  Sure I can dig up a few gripes, but quite honestly that was one of the best weeks of my life, right up there with the one I wrote about when I started my trip a year ago.  That’s sort of the point, quit your day job, sell everything you own and awesome things happen.

Sure, it’s damn near impossible to sleep when the large Stampede crowds don’t disperse until midnight, then although there are 10 times less stragglers wandering out of the bars like Nashville North, they happen to be 10 times drunker and 10 times louder, which is to be expected.  And it doesn’t help when you have events at 6 or 7 AM three days in a row to start the Stampede coupled with about a dozen of your 20 “unique experiences” in the same time frame, but I get it now.

Austin Meier is nails

While I only gained between 250 and 300 Twitter followers and only 88 people have watched my video of riding a chuckwagon (watch it here in HD), the Stampede thought it was a rip roaring success after I did 6 different media spots on Tuesday (good CTV one here).  Apparently Prince Will & Kate provided an estimated 2 to 3 million dollars in free press coverage for the Stampede, so I’m going to run with the assumption they came close to getting their $5000 value in prizes back from me, especially considering they probably only cost the Stampede $2500.  Hell, I already sold the iPhone 4 for twice as much as my “salary”.

But looking back and putting it all in a nutshell, I met Olympic Gold medalists and the second ranked bull rider in North America, rode 65 km/h in a horse-drawn wagon, got to stand on the chuckwagon track during a race and even helped Clint the rodeo clown load up the t-shirt cannon only to watch him shatter a spotlight and spray the crowd with glass.  And this of course glosses over the countless beers and countless pretty ladies.

Incredible colour

If I was going to let fly with one complaint, it was simply being too busy to sit down and enjoy myself and not having the time to create some more of my own content just being myself.  Being told they’re called “product mentions” not “plugs” while getting a list of sponsors to shout out I thought somewhat damaged my credibility as well.  But hey, it’s the first year there’s ever been an Ultimate Stampede Intern, and I sure as hell hope to weasel my way back into future Stampedes in some capacity or another.

Expect a few more post-mortems and me to finally finish editing my Stampede epic pizza time video in the next week or two.  Thanks for following!

item.title: Calgary Stampede 2011: Baby Steps
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: How sad is this, I could have got in no line, no cover at Cowboys tonight and decided to save it for another day! I haven’t been in this much sensory overload wandering the Stampede grounds since I watched Transformers 3, and that’s saying a lot, that was almost aneurism territory. I figured rather than [...]
item.content:encoded:
How sad is this, I could have got in no line, no cover at Cowboys tonight and decided to save it for another day!

Why does this look so familiar?

I haven’t been in this much sensory overload wandering the Stampede grounds since I watched Transformers 3, and that’s saying a lot, that was almost aneurism territory.  I figured rather than waking up early for the pre-parade breakfast and puking on the Marshall’s shoes, I might actually just ease into this whole thing rather than emptying my clip on day 1.

I’m already pretty in with the Stampede Queen and Princesses having my second line after meeting them be “I like my hat bent wrong, I’m not taking it off for you to fix because I haven’t showered today.”  In Amarillo Texas that would come across as smooth, I still need to readjust.  With one of my 20 events being “How to shop for a hat and boots” coupled with my clothing store gift certificate, maybe I can get Eliza Doolittle on errrbody and pretty myself up a touch.  Maybe.

Wait, that's my name

But yeah, baby steps.  I’m still too frightened by the horrific Stampede powers I posses to use them for evil or good.  During my backstage tour with the Young Canadians before the Grandstand Show, one location in the story was described to me as the Garden of Imagination.  I later referred to it as Imaginationland…which is NOT the same thing.  Thank God nobody coordinating the event watches much South Park.

And seriously, I tweeted about it, but the scene with the acrobat was as priceless as it gets.  I was sitting in the Grandstand Show Committee trailer while they hammered out the last details of the first dress rehearsal and in walked a tall long-haired guy asking if he could get into Nashville North after the show and was told they’d really cracked down on that the last few years, which I can attest to not even being able to jump line as the Ultimate Intern.  I always tell people I’m terrible at names but amazing with faces, so after a minute I chimed in “hey, are you an acrobat?  Did you perform on Granville Island last summer?”  Sort of shrugging it off but still excited I recognized him, he piped back “yeah, glad you saw it, lemme go get you these promotion cards we have!”

Ohhhh, that pic from 11 months ago!

So he comes back and gives me a card and I’m just staring at it continuously thinking that looks EXACTLY like the shot I took on Granville Island.  Then I flip over the card and it has photography credits from Blimpy Backgammon.  Apparently I’ve seen so much in the last year I completely forgot e-mailing him my pics and providing the quotable on the back “Equilibrium Circus is ridiculously talented!”  At least I still stand by it, because dammit, they are, expect Twitter updates on shows they plan to do in town, totally worth checking out.

item.title: Calgary Stampede 2011: Interview with the paper
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: “I have a mission for you, should you chose to accept it” the Calgary Herald reporter asked over the phone. “Will my computer explode in 5 seconds if I do?” I quipped back. Her silent deadpan threw a wet blanket on what for me was a pretty sharp line, apparently she just wanted a headshot [...]
item.content:encoded:
“I have a mission for you, should you chose to accept it” the Calgary Herald reporter asked over the phone.

“Will my computer explode in 5 seconds if I do?” I quipped back.

That's me!

Her silent deadpan threw a wet blanket on what for me was a pretty sharp line, apparently she just wanted a headshot sent in for the article.  “She” being Lea Storry, perhaps the best journalist name in history.

Not used to my newfound world of press handlers and having 12 minutes of dialogue distilled into 3 sentences of sound bites, I was curious what the end result would be.  It’s more straightforward than what I’d write to tell my own story, but probably makes more sense given I answered “to get to the crossroads in the Mississippi river delta” as my motivation to sell everything I own and live in an RV.  I suppose this is my fault as I’m trying to ease into my new role with kid gloves and held back my usual quotables like “I ain’t going to work on Maggie’s farm no more” or “outer space, think about it!”

I ain't rappin for God, I ain't rappin for money

On the adjacent page in the paper is a twice as long life story of some Christian rapper Arturo Caballero who calls himself MashetiMoses, apparently given this “rap name” by God after fasting and praying.  Too bad I just finished four days of fasting in the desert and emerged named the exact same, otherwise I’d get more press.

I’m not sure if it was taken into account when selecting the Calgary Stampede 2011 intern contest winner, but you really do need to have a screw or two loose to want to live in an RV on the Stampede grounds for 10 days, and I’m in a pretty unique spot already living in an RV and being short more than a few marbles.  While writing this at the breakfast table I came to the conclusion that if I get to interview Kevin Costner, I’m going to challenge him to a kung fu battle and overdub it poorly as a short film.

Presumably the Stampede’s goal with this internship is to get as much exposure as possible, and I figure I’ll best be able to help with that if I bring a bit of edge.  But don’t worry, I’ll still be wearing pants for the TV interviews.

item.title: Ultimate Calgary Stampede Intern
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Every day until June 17th vote for Blimpy as the Ultimate Calgary Stampede Intern! It’s a fantastic contest being run by the Calgary Stampede and if I win I get to live on the grounds for 10 days in my own trailer with 24/7 backstage access to blog about all kinds of fun and ridiculous [...]
item.content:encoded:
Every day until June 17th vote for Blimpy as the Ultimate Calgary Stampede Intern!  It’s a fantastic contest being run by the Calgary Stampede and if I win I get to live on the grounds for 10 days in my own trailer with 24/7 backstage access to blog about all kinds of fun and ridiculous stuff!  You can also watch my Calgary Stampede Intern video on YouTube, but please make sure to click the link to vote every day until June 17th.

The video itself goes through all the reasons why I think I’m qualified to show everyone a rip-roaring good time and I really appreciate everyone’s support.  Plus, you’ll be paid back in spades if I’m lucky enough to win as I promise it will be 10 days of absolute hilarity.  As the Ultimate Calgary Stampede Intern I’ll be able to cover 20 different events at the Stampede on an iPhone 4 while drafting up videos, blog posts and tweets.

Also, I’m really enjoying the chance to improve in filming and editing videos, so just think what kind of a show I can come up with when the grounds are full of people!  As you can see from the one lady at the end of my video, the Calgary Stampede seems to attract lots of excitable characters, so mix in the rodeo, some BBQ and sunny July heat and it’s guaranteed to be a great ride.

Thanks again to everyone for following Blimpy and I’d be forever grateful if you could pass the link along to anyone you can think of!

item.content:encoded:
I’m trying to get voted in as the Calgary Stampede Ultimate Social Media Intern and it would be a huge boost if people could vote for me every day from now until June 17th and repost that link wherever possible.  See the newest Blimpy video and vote for me here please!!  (Oh, and as usual it’s cooler in HD, this time only 720p…and if you want to read what the contest is for check here)

Not only will you be helping me get backstage access and my own trailer to a 10 day, 24 hour carnival of awesomeness, you’ll be helping to ensure all kinds of ridiculous content gets generated come July!

Quite the difference

The video was crafted in exactly 24 hours with my friend filming and me starring and editing.  I’m kind of a fan of the 60 second idea because it forces me to not ramble.  Also, we used a new Technicolor picture style on my camera where it films everything super flat and I have to add all the saturation, contrast and sharpness back in post, but as you can see from the before and after screenshot, I think it’s worth it and will likely be using this style for all future videos.

Also, I apologize in advance, but expect to see a lot of Facebook and Twitter updates this week reminding you to vote every day.  All we have to do is make the top 10 and the judges hand-pick a winner from there, and I legitamitly like our chances!

I hope you’re looking forward to a summer of awesomeness as much as I am!

Remember to VOTE HERE every day until June 17!!!!

item.title: Texas is bigger than France
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: I have had this fridge magnet since my early days working for a Texas based oil services company in 2006, and only now do I realize how true it is. While I believe it was first crafted during the “War on France” via Freedom Fries because they’re a bunch of pacifist, non-Iraqi murdering jerks, it [...]
item.content:encoded:
I have had this fridge magnet since my early days working for a Texas based oil services company in 2006, and only now do I realize how true it is.  While I believe it was first crafted during the “War on France” via Freedom Fries because they’re a bunch of pacifist, non-Iraqi murdering jerks, it also well-symbolizes the “everything is bigger in Texas” mantra, which includes Texas itself.  And you should see the Republic of Texas map from 1864, now that place was big.  However, these days whenever someone tells me I should “check out Austin because it’s cool” for the umpteenth time, a little bit of me dies inside.

Texas used to be REALLY big

The drive from Amarillo to Austin is roughly 550 miles, or in Bessie-speak $200 of gas each way, which adds up to half a month’s budget in Blimpy-speak.  I am much closer to Denver (not that I intend to go there either).  Hell, just the Texas panhandle is the same size as most states (and with less water than probably any of them too).

When I was near Sedona Arizona, for the first time I saw a weather forecast calling for “Dust”.  In Amarillo it calls for “Fire Weather”.  Not knowing what the hell this is, I Wikipedia it and find their example is a weather advisory…from Amarillo Texas.  By 7 PM I see a large smoke plume coming from a dusty dry field 10 miles away quickly spreading due to the 55 mph winds and read on the news of evacuations to the south.  The actual definition I believe is humidity below 10%, temperature above 90 F and winds greater than 40 mph.  I also realized quite suddenly around this point in time the two tornados that killed people on May 24th in Canton and Piedmont Oklahoma are only 200 miles from here, so when the skies started turning green as well, I actually got kind of nervous.

Maybe this is all happening because Repent Amarillo is right and it has nothing to do with global warming?  For the uninitiated, Repent Amarillo is an organization that deems businesses in the surrounding area immoral, then tries to shut them down with tactics ranging from calling the fire marshal to camping outside with cameras to terrorize the patrons.  I only made it to three of the spots on their map accidentally, I will investigate more when I return.

Fridge magnet FTW

I also found out the legendary “Dude, you have no Koran” was born right here in Amarillo because Repent Amarillo is apparently buddies with Terry Jones.  The facebook group Amarillo Citizens Against Repent Amarillo jumped 3500 members in one day after the event, which is not only hilarious, but uplifting that not everyone is as crazy as you think even in the so-called Bible Belt.  Although I did get a nice reply from the editor of the Amarillo Globe telling me they wouldn’t publish my letter refuting one from a pastor the day before who claimed the Bible was “undeniable scientific fact” because my retort was “too provocative”.

That said, a lot of small towns in rural Oregon and Northern California are far more horrifyingly stereotypical American than Amarillo is.  I’m convinced anywhere with at least 250,000 people must have something going on, and the Walmarts here are on the outskirts of town, have a lot less people riding motorized scooters when they can obviously walk and they sell whole wheat bread.  Honestly, the place is genuinely complex, they got layers and stuff!
